sheet-2-1.description: Sheet 2 of the 1927 Dunellen atlas, main map, covering the western edge of the borough where the older Bound Brook Road lines run diagonally across the sheet. The sheet is drawn with north toward the upper right. Bound Brook Road crosses the middle of the sheet from upper left to lower right, with Front lying parallel to it on the north and Sanford Avenue crossing both at the right. Long narrow lots with scattered frame dwellings are laid out on both sides of Bound Brook Road, and a pipe line runs beside the street. Private Road runs diagonally from the lower middle toward the upper right, passing a long yellow building marked for 40 autos. North Avenue crosses the lower right of the sheet, with a regular row of dwellings along its south side. In the lower left lies the works of R. Hoe and Company, manufacturers of printing presses: a machine shop, a large store house for blooms, small steel and iron, a frame building, offices, an engine room, a stock room and a box shop with pattern storage. The works carry sprinkler marks and a note giving the private fire protection, watchman's clock, lighting and city water supply. A reservoir of 700,000 gallons lies north of the works, and the Central Railroad of New Jersey runs along the bottom edge. A brook follows the left edge. The heavy-bordered box at the left centre is a separate inset showing a foundry of the same firm and is not part of this part. Block numbers 62, 63, 74 and 85 appear, and the sheet adjoins sheets 3 and 8.
notes: Chestnut Street on sheet 3 continues as the street shown here as Private Road; OpenStreetMap names it Pulaski Street (not verified for this sheet).
A brook is lettered along the left edge; its name could not be read with confidence and is left out.
Modern Bound Brook Road is realigned west of Sanford Avenue and does not follow the straight street drawn here; only the Sanford Avenue junctions are used.

Map, 50 ft. West end: Bound Brook Road, Sanford Av, Front St. Part 1 main map anchored on one junction (Bound Brook Road / Sanford Avenue); part 2 inset (R. Hoe & Co. foundry premises, own north arrow) unplaced.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: R. Hoe & Co. foundry premises (no street junction; foundry lies west of sheet 2 and is drawn on no placed neighbour; needs carried points from sheet-11-1, which draws the R. Hoe works in place at its top left (sheet-11-1 is itself weak), or parcel corners of the works site).

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 of the 1927 Dunellen atlas shows the western part of the borough, with north toward the upper right. On the left and centre the older diagonal street pattern prevails: Dunellen Avenue, Front and Bound Brook Road run from upper left to lower right, crossed by Sanford Avenue at the upper left, and long narrow lots with scattered frame dwellings lie between them. At the right the plan changes to a rectangular grid based on Madison Avenue North, which runs down the right edge, with Dunellen Avenue, Front and North Avenue meeting it and blocks of detached dwellings between. St. Nicholas Greek Catholic Church stands on the east side of the Madison Avenue block between Front and North Avenue, and a garage and auto repair shop, a cement block manufactory, a grain warehouse and the premises of the Dunellen Coal and Grain Company lie near the lower right, where Bound Brook Road meets North Avenue. North Avenue crosses the lower part of the sheet, with a row of small dwellings on its south side, and Chestnut runs diagonally from Bound Brook Road to North Avenue. The Central Railroad of New Jersey and a spur track appear at the bottom edge. Several buildings are marked as dwellings of two storeys, with a few yellow shed outbuildings and one or two brick buildings. Block numbers 56, 63, 74, 85 and 86 are printed, and the sheet adjoins sheets 2, 4, 8, 11 and 12.
notes: Chestnut is Pulaski Street in OpenStreetMap.
Madison Avenue North is Madison Avenue today; the street centre lies at the right edge of the sheet and only its left half is drawn.
Bound Brook Road junctions with Chestnut and North Avenue were not detected and are not used.
Map, 50 ft. Old diagonal street pattern at left, Madison Av N grid at right; Chestnut St = Pulaski Street. Madison Av centreline at the sheet edge.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 of the 1927 Dunellen atlas shows the centre of the borough between Madison Avenue North on the left and Lincoln Avenue on the right, at 50 feet to an inch. The sheet is drawn with north toward the upper right. Three east-west streets cross it: Dunellen Avenue across the top, Front through the middle and North Avenue near the bottom. Between them lie regular blocks of detached frame dwellings with outbuildings, mostly two storeys, with rear lot lines running the width of each block. On Madison Avenue North at the left of the lower block stands Hosfords Theatre, a brick building with lobby and lights and heat by steam, with stores beside it. The J. O. U. A. M. Hall, a bowling alley, a filling station, a plaster mill and an oven building, and areas of scattered lumber and lumber piles lie south of North Avenue. Bound Brook Road enters at the lower left, Grove Street is lettered at the foot of the sheet, and the Central Railroad of New Jersey runs across the bottom as a broad band of tracks. Water pipe lines of six and eight inches are marked in the streets. Block numbers 57, 64 and 87 are printed. The sheet adjoins sheets 3 on the left, 5 on the right, 9 above and 12 below.
notes: Lincoln Avenue is lettered vertically along the right side as Lincoln Av.
Reading written from the 1600 px overview at its printed size; spellings of building names were not checked on full-resolution crops.
Map, 50 ft. Dunellen Av, Front St, North Av between Madison Av and Lincoln Av; CRR of NJ along the bottom. Pilot sheet.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 of the 1927 Dunellen atlas covers the business centre of the borough between Lincoln Avenue on the left and Washington Avenue North on the right, at 50 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right. Dunellen Avenue crosses the top, Front the middle and North Avenue the lower part. The blocks along Dunellen Avenue and Front are lined with detached frame dwellings, while the North Avenue frontage between Lincoln and Washington Avenues is a continuous row of stores, many of brick, including the First National Bank near the middle and a club house of the B. P. O. E. on Washington Avenue North above the avenue. South of North Avenue, Prospect Avenue runs diagonally to the railroad past the Municipal Offices and the fire station of Defender Company No. 1. A park occupies the block bounded by North Avenue, Prospect Avenue and Washington Avenue South, and the Central Railroad of New Jersey passenger depot and freight house stand beside the many tracks of the main line at the bottom of the sheet. Water pipe lines are marked in the streets, and the sheet number 5 and block numbers 58, 65, 87 and 88 are printed. The sheet adjoins sheet 4 on the left, sheet 6 on the right, sheet 9 above and sheet 12 below.
notes: Washington Avenue North is North Washington Avenue today.
Reading written from the 1600 px overview at its printed size; building names were not checked on full-resolution crops.
Map, 50 ft. Business centre, Lincoln Av to Washington Av N.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 of the 1927 Dunellen atlas shows the blocks east of Washington Avenue as far as Jackson Avenue, at 50 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right. Front crosses the upper part and North Avenue the middle, both lined with detached frame dwellings, with Hotel Charlotte at the corner of Front and Washington Avenue North. Along the south side of North Avenue near Washington Avenue stand the post office, a garage and a row of stores, and the Dunellen Lumber and Coal Company yard lies beside the railroad. South of North Avenue the Central Railroad of New Jersey fills the sheet with tracks: sidings, a roundhouse with turntable and a boiler house, and the long main line. The large Art Color Printing Company works fills the south part of the sheet between Washington Avenue South and the edge, a brick building with press rooms, bindery, paper storage, shipping and platform. South Avenue is lettered along the bottom, with New Market Road at the lower left corner. Block numbers 59, 66, 89 and 95 are printed, and a water pipe runs in the streets. The sheet adjoins sheet 5 on the left, sheet 7 on the right, sheet 10 above and sheets 12 and 13 below.
notes: Washington Avenue North is North Washington Avenue today.
The drawn railroad lies about 15 m from the modern line in the second-pass check; the railroad corridor was left in the mask.
Reading written from the 1600 px overview at its printed size; building names were not checked on full-resolution crops.
Map, 50 ft. Washington Av N to Jackson Av; railroad and Art Color Printing Co. Drawn railroad about 15 m from the modern line.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 of the 1927 Dunellen atlas covers the eastern end of the borough between Jackson Avenue on the left and Jefferson Avenue on the right, at 50 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right. Front crosses the upper part of the sheet and North Avenue the middle, with detached frame dwellings on the lots between and a few brick and stone buildings with sheds at the east end of North Avenue. Jefferson Avenue along the right edge is the boundary with the city of Plainfield, lettered with a note to see the Plainfield map, and New Market is lettered at the lower right beside a second street, 2nd Street. South of North Avenue the Central Railroad of New Jersey runs across the sheet in many tracks, marked as full of tracks, with the plant of the Gulf Refining Company, with its storage buildings, set beside the lines near the left. A large brick works appears at the lower left corner. South Avenue is lettered at the bottom. Block numbers 60, 67, 89 and 95 are printed, and water pipe lines run in the streets. The sheet adjoins sheet 6 on the left and Plainfield on the right, sheet 10 above and sheet 13 below.
notes: Jefferson Avenue is the borough boundary with the city of Plainfield; the street centre lies near the right edge.
The drawn railroad lies about 12 m from the modern line in the first-pass check.
Reading written from the 1600 px overview at its printed size; building names were not checked on full-resolution crops.
Map, 50 ft. Jackson Av to Jefferson Av (Plainfield line). Drawn railroad about 12 m from the modern line.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 of the 1927 Dunellen atlas is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and shows the north-western part of the borough, with north toward the upper right. The upper half is mostly vacant platted land, with the unopened lines of 6th Street, Mountain View Terrace and 4th Street running east-west to Madison Avenue North at the right edge, and block numbers 15, 18 and 22 within. The lower half is a built-up district laid out in long narrow lots on diagonal streets: Schwartz Place, 1st Street, 2nd Street and 3rd Street run from upper left to lower right and are crossed by Sanford Avenue, with Dunellen Avenue, Front and Bound Brook Road at the foot of the sheet. Detached frame dwellings stand along these streets. Part of the third street, 3rd Street, is marked not open near the right. The left margin is lettered Middlesex Borough, with the borough limits running irregularly up the sheet, and Green Brook with its borough limits appears at the top right. The sheet adjoins sheet 2 and sheet 3 below and sheet 9 to the right.
notes: Only the Madison Avenue North and Mountain View Terrace junction is used for placement; 1st to 3rd Streets and the lower blocks did not agree with the modern streets (fits of 5 to 10 m RMSE).
Madison Avenue North is Madison Avenue today.
Reading written from the 1600 px overview at its printed size; building and street names were not checked on full-resolution crops.
Map, 100 ft. Northwest, unopened streets at top, platted blocks (1st to 3rd St, Schwartz Pl) below that do not match modern streets; anchored on Madison Av / Mountain View Terrace.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers the northern residential part of Dunellen, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It is a full-page sheet of four-block-wide city grid between Madison Avenue North on the west side and Washington Avenue North on the east, with Dunellen Avenue closing the sheet at the bottom and the Mountain View Terrace tier of lots near the top. Cross streets run from 1st Street at the lower part of the sheet up through 2nd, 3rd and 4th Streets. Lincoln Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet. Housing is overwhelmingly small frame dwellings (coloured yellow) set on narrow lots with a few brick or stone buildings; the lower blocks hold two churches and a school, among them St. John's Evangelical Lutheran church and school and St. John's Roman Catholic church, and Lincoln School stands on the bottom edge. The upper third of the sheet is thinly built, with large undivided blocks marked not open, and at the very top a brook and the boundary of North Plainfield Township run across. A compass rose and a printed scale bar sit in the upper left and bottom left. The sheet continues on sheet 10 at the right and sheet 8 at the left, and on sheets 4 and 5 below.
notes: Reading made on overview-resolution crops (1600 px wide) rather than full-resolution crops; names and spellings should be rechecked at full size. Street names are given as printed with abbreviations expanded.
Modern names: Madison Avenue North is Madison Avenue and Washington Avenue North is North Washington Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Map, 100 ft. North Dunellen, Madison/Lincoln/Washington Av between Dunellen Av and Mountain View Terrace.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers the northeast part of Dunellen at 100 feet to an inch, between Washington Avenue on the west and Jefferson Avenue on the east, from Dunellen Avenue at the bottom up to Mountain View Terrace and the brook near the top. The built-up area is a band of two or three rows of blocks along 1st, 2nd and 3rd Streets with small frame dwellings, with a larger park or open ground block marked Park west of Park Place and several undivided blocks to the east that are only sparsely built. Park Place, Jackson Avenue and Jefferson Avenue run north and south. The upper half of the sheet is mostly open land cut by a looping stream, Green Brook, with the line of North Plainfield Township shown along the top and a note at the right edge directing the reader to the Plainfield map. The scale bar is at lower left and the compass rose at the centre top. Washington Avenue and Dunellen Avenue are shared with sheets 9 and 5, and the sheet continues south onto sheets 6 and 7.
notes: Reading made on overview-resolution crops (1600 px wide) rather than full-resolution crops; names and spellings should be rechecked at full size.
Printed legend at the right edge refers to a Plainfield map for the area beyond Jefferson Avenue.
Modern name: Washington Avenue is North Washington Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Map, 100 ft. Northeast Dunellen, Washington to Jefferson Av, Green Brook at top.

sheet-11-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 11 is the main map of the sheet, covering the district between South Avenue at the top and Center Street at the bottom in the New Market section of Piscataway Township, adjoining the south side of Dunellen. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the sheet turned so that streets run diagonally across the page. Long narrow lots front on Levgar, Hall, Chestnut and Madison Avenue South, with Walnut and Lehigh crossing them, and Fairview Avenue and Prospect Avenue run along the right side. Most of the area is open farmland or subdivided lots with few buildings, the houses being scattered and small; a brook flows across the upper part from South Avenue towards the east. At the top right edge a cluster of regularly drawn blocks of Dunellen shows lots numbered in the 500s and 600s along South Avenue, and the borough boundary is marked in dashes through the middle of the sheet. A compass rose and scale bar are at the bottom. A boxed inset at the bottom left corner is a separate part (part 2). The sheet adjoins sheets 12, 14 and 19.
notes: Reading made on overview-resolution crops (1600 px wide) rather than full-resolution crops; names and spellings should be rechecked at full size.

Printed Madison Avenue South is the modern South Madison Avenue and printed Fairview Avenue the modern Fairview Avenue; the street marked not named west of Madison has no modern match. Placed from ten junctions, two of them hand-read on Center Street.
Map, 100 ft. New Market district, turned about 33 deg; part 1 main map (two points, helmert), part 2 boxed inset at lower left anchored on Center St / Hall.

sheet-11-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 11 is a boxed inset at the lower left corner of the sheet, outlined by a heavy line and drawn square to the page with its own north arrow. It shows a small block of lots in the New Market section of Piscataway Township at 100 feet to an inch, bounded by Levgar on the west, Center along the south side and Hall at the east, with the borough limits drawn as a dash-dot line along Hall. A block of numbered lots, 1901 to 1907, fronts on Center, and a few small frame and brick dwellings stand on them; most of the inset is open land. The inset is marked with the number 11 and the sheet number 102 beside the block. Anthony Avenue and Webster Avenue are named on the main map just beyond the outline on the north and east, and Clay Avenue at the bottom. A short scale bar for the inset runs along the bottom right.
notes: Reading made on overview-resolution crops (1600 px wide) rather than full-resolution crops; names and spellings should be rechecked at full size.
Placed on two hand-read control points (Center with Levgar, Center with Hall); low confidence.
Map, 100 ft. New Market district, turned about 33 deg; part 1 main map (two points, helmert), part 2 boxed inset at lower left anchored on Center St / Hall.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers the district south of Dunellen's centre where the borough meets New Market, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. South Avenue crosses the top, with the Morecraft Coal Co. yard at the upper left edge, and diagonal streets run through the sheet: Madison Avenue South and Fairview Avenue at the left, Prospect Avenue and Argus Place through the middle, with Walnut, Grove and Whittier Avenue crossing them, and New Market Road, Orange, Penfield Place and Oak Parkway (Culhane Place) in the right half down to Washington Avenue South on the east edge. Housing is small frame dwellings on narrow lots with some brick houses, and the Whittier School stands at the centre right. A small brook and a railroad water pipe line cross the left side. Street junctions are marked by dots. The sheet's lower part is labelled Borough of Dunellen with a boundary running along the bottom, below which Tabor appears. A compass rose is at the top right. It adjoins sheets 4, 5, 6, 11, 13, 14 and 16.
notes: Reading made on overview-resolution crops (1600 px wide) rather than full-resolution crops; names and spellings should be rechecked at full size.
Oak Parkway is shown with Culhane Place in parentheses as an alternative name.
Modern names follow OpenStreetMap: Madison Avenue South is South Madison Avenue, Washington Avenue South is South Washington Avenue.
Map, 100 ft. Dunellen / New Market border south of South Av.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers the southeast corner of Dunellen's built-up area, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. A strip of housing lies along the left edge on both sides of Washington Avenue, between New Market Road at the top and Walnut at the bottom, with Columbia, Orange Place, Penfield Place, Oak Parkway (Culhane Place) and Maple Avenue branching off. The rest of the sheet is mostly open land with undivided blocks, crossed by West 3rd Street (not open) in the upper part and West 4th Street along the foot, where a row of houses runs along the street under a borough boundary line. Kline Place cuts across at the lower centre and New Market is lettered along the right edge. South Avenue is shown along the top margin. Houses are small frame buildings with a few brick dwellings, and the Dunellen borough limits follow the boundary lines. A compass rose is near the upper centre and the scale bar is at the bottom right. The sheet adjoins sheets 6, 7, 12, 16, 17 and 18.
notes: Reading made on overview-resolution crops (1600 px wide) rather than full-resolution crops; names and spellings should be rechecked at full size.
Placed on seven control points; five of them lie along Washington Avenue, so rotation and scale rest mainly on that street (leave-one-out about 4 m).
Washington Avenue here is South Washington Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Map, 100 ft. Southeast Dunellen along Washington Av S; much open land; control along two streets.

sheet-14-1.description: Sheet 14, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, shows the New Market section of Piscataway Township just east of Dunellen. The map is a grid of residential blocks bounded on the west by Longfellow Avenue and on the east by New Market Road, with Center Street, marked as the borough limits, running across the middle of the sheet. North of Center Street the blocks along Whittier Avenue and Prospect Avenue are sparsely built, with scattered dwellings, a few poultry sheds and the Holy Innocents Protestant Episcopal Church. South of it the blocks between Longfellow, Fairview, Prospect and Whittier carry rows of numbered frame dwellings on Church, Dutchman and Edwards Avenue, and the 7th Day Baptist Church and the 1st Baptist Church stand on Whittier Street, the latter with auto sheds, bowling alleys and a hall beside it. Union Street closes the sheet on the south. At the bottom left the Lehigh Valley Railroad crosses diagonally, with the Pure Asphalt Products Co. works, makers of Red Battery Wax and Sewer Seal, beside Bound Brook. The upper left corner, separated by a heavy line and not covered by this part, shows the Battelle & Fenwick saltpetre works. North lies toward the upper right.
notes: The notch at the top left of the page (Battelle & Fenwick works, Edwards Av., Longfellow Rv, Webster Rv) is drawn at another location and is not part of this part's mask.
Reading made from the 1600 px overview; names not checked on every full-resolution crop.
Map, 100 ft. New Market; part 1 main; notch at top left (part 2, Battelle & Fenwick works) unplaced.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: notch at top left: Battelle & Fenwick works (Edwards Av, Longfellow, Webster) (no surviving street junction; needs step 6b from sheet-11 or parcel corners).

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 covers the centre of the New Market section of Piscataway Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Bound Brook crosses the upper part from the left, with New Market Pond to its right and the Lehigh Valley railroad tracks and the Central Railroad of New Jersey running east and west across the top. New Market Road and Stelton Road run north and south through the middle, with a settled strip along Lake View Avenue, William Street (also Bound Brook Avenue) and Day Avenue. Industry includes C. E. Kelly Co. hay, grain and feed and Middlesex Milling Co. near the brook, and the New Market Public School is at the lower centre. The streets south of the brook are regular, named Hoe, Day, Nelson, School, Tabb and Hopkinson Avenues, with Montgomery and Kossuth on the vertical lines, and Terrace Court, Pershing Place, William Place and Lewis Place are short side streets. Most lots are small with scattered frame dwellings and open blocks, particularly in the lower left. The compass rose is at the top and the scale bar at lower right. The sheet adjoins sheets 14, 16 and 19.
notes: Reading made on overview-resolution crops (1600 px wide) rather than full-resolution crops; names and spellings should be rechecked at full size.
A drawn Lehigh Line railroad corridor sits 17 m from its OpenStreetMap line in the detector's check.
Modern names: Lake View Avenue is Lakeview Avenue; Kossuth is Kossuth Street; Montgomery is Montgomery Street.
Map, 100 ft. New Market centre, Bound Brook, New Market Pond, Stelton Road; Lehigh Valley line drawn about 17 m from its modern line.

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16, at 100 feet to an inch, covers the New Market section of Piscataway Township east of Dunellen. The left edge follows New Market Road and the Borough of Dunellen limit. In the northwest are large undivided lots, a ditch and Tabor, a private way, with scattered dwellings. West of Washington Avenue S. a regular grid of blocks lies between Central Place and Van Winkle Place, cut by Valmere Avenue and Victoria Avenue, with numbered dwellings on every lot. The middle of the sheet is crossed by Sherwood Drive and by 7th Street (Vail Avenue), with a printing and electric power building in blue near it, and numbered streets 8th, 9th, 10th and 11th run across the south. Washington Avenue S. and Kline Boulevard run diagonally from the upper right, and the blocks between them are cut by W. 7th Street, Chestnut, Beech and Olive. Adrian Avenue closes the sheet on the east. The northeast quadrant holds long narrow farm strips with few buildings. North lies toward the upper right.
notes: Reading made from the 1600 px overview; names not checked on every full-resolution crop.
Map, 100 ft. New Market east of Dunellen.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17, at 100 feet to an inch, shows the New Market and Arbor sections along the Borough of Dunellen limit. The map is turned about 40 degrees, with north toward the upper left. A broad diagonal avenue, Walnut Boulevard, runs from lower left to upper right and meets Kline Boulevard, W. 4th Street and W. 7th Street, which run vertically on the page. West of Kline Boulevard are many narrow deep lots with numbered dwellings, a few outbuildings and a fire department building. East of W. 7th Street the sheet shows the Arbor tract, with Henry Place, Albert Place, Hughes Terrace and Mansfield Road laid out beside one another, a short row of dwellings on Mansfield Road and large vacant blocks marked Not Named. At the upper right Meister, Russell Court, Walnut Street Extension and the short numbered places 2nd to 6th lie at an angle to the main grid. Beech Avenue, Olive Avenue and Pelham cross at the lower right. A compass rose in the middle right shows the turned north.
notes: Sheet is turned about 40 degrees from north-up. Reading made from the 1600 px overview; names not checked on every full-resolution crop.
Map, 100 ft, turned about -41 deg; New Market and Arbor.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18, at 100 feet to an inch, covers the Arbor section of Piscataway Township at the City of Plainfield limit and the Borough of Dunellen limit. The map is turned about 40 degrees, with north toward the upper left; a dash-dot line marks the City of Plainfield boundary diagonally across the upper left and another marks the Borough of Dunellen limit along the bottom. At the left, blocks between 2nd Street and W. 3rd Street are cut by Oak Place, Chestnut Place, Poplar Place and Hazelwood Place and carry numbered dwellings. Rock Avenue crosses the top. At the top right Mabel, Ann, Miller and Leslie lie between small farm lots, and Elk runs diagonally toward Arbor. The centre is mostly large lots marked Not Open. Along the right edge W. 4th Street has a line of dwellings, and Star runs near the bottom. At the lower left is the American Cable Co. wire rope works with drawing and winding buildings, tanks and a water tank. A note reads Also shown on Plainfield Map.
notes: Sheet is turned about 40 degrees from north-up. Reading made from the 1600 px overview; names not checked on every full-resolution crop.
Map, 100 ft, turned about -39 deg; Arbor, Plainfield limit.

sheet-19-1.description: Sheet 19, main part, at 100 feet to an inch, shows the Arbor section of Piscataway Township. The map is turned about 40 degrees, with north toward the upper left. Rock Avenue runs across the middle and W. 6th Street, W. 7th Street, Meister and Quincy run vertically on the page across it. At the upper left Evona Avenue and Division Avenue run diagonally through a fan of long narrow lots, with Lewis Court, Elysian Court, Rushmore Avenue, Clark Place and Irving Place between them. The Arbor Public School, a pink-coloured brick building, stands west of Lester Place. Kline Boulevard runs along the lower left and a diagonal avenue runs through blocks with a brass foundry and rows of numbered dwellings. In the lower right Harold Place, Walnut, Lake Court and Russel Court lie among large vacant blocks cut into narrow strips. A heavy line at the top right separates the New Market works inset, which is its own part. Most lots are narrow and unbuilt apart from the left edge.
notes: Sheet is turned about 40 degrees from north-up. Reading made from the 1600 px overview; names not checked on every full-resolution crop.
Map, 100 ft, turned about -41 deg; part 1 main (Arbor); part 2 box at top right (Levering & Garrigues works, north up) anchored on Howard St / South Av.

sheet-19-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 19 is the box at the top right, headed New Market, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the top of the page. It shows the Levering & Garrigues Co. structural iron works, with a large pink-coloured machine and erecting shop, a forge shop, stock room, templet shop, store houses and cranes. Long travelling craneways with dashed outlines run across and beside the works, and two railroad sidings curve in from the south to serve them. A note at the bottom reads No Exposure. South Avenue runs diagonally across the upper left, with Howard (Byrom) running along the west of the works and Levgar at the right edge. A note on night watchman, clock, power, steam and electric lighting and fire protection is printed beside the works. Most of the surrounding ground is vacant.
notes: Placed from one junction (Howard Street / South Avenue) with the atlas scale and north up; low confidence in rotation. Reading made from the 1600 px overview; names not checked on every full-resolution crop.
